# A/W Design System

> Design tokens and documentation for the A/W design system, generated from Figma (Foundation – UI 2). Use the CSS classes and custom properties below instead of hard-coded values.

This file is generated by `npm run tokens` (scripts/build-tokens.mjs). Do not edit by hand.

## Typography

Type tokens for body text and headings, organised around t-shirt sizes — large, medium, small — to make it easy to build multiple levels of hierarchy.

Font: Inter (variable weights). Rules:

- Always set text with a .text-* class (or its CSS variables). Never hard-code font-size, font-weight, line-height or letter-spacing.
- Use headings for hierarchy and body styles for content; don't use a heading style just to make text bigger.
- Use the strong variant of a body style for emphasis within the same size, not a heading style.
- Display is reserved for onboarding and heavily branded moments — at most one per view.
- Pair type with semantic text color tokens (e.g. --color-text-default, --color-text-secondary), never primitives.

| Class | Figma style | Size/Line height (px) | Weight | Letter spacing | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.text-heading-display` | heading/display | 48/56 | 550 | -0.03em | To create continuity with our logged-out marketing views, we sparingly use Inter for onboarding and other heavily branded moments. |
| `.text-heading-large` | heading/large | 24/32 | 550 | -0.017em | Our largest heading size, reserved for elements like the primary page title within large views. |
| `.text-heading-medium` | heading/medium | 15/25 | 550 | -0.005em | Section headings within a page or large panel. |
| `.text-heading-small` | heading/small | 13/22 | 550 | -0.0025em | Headings for compact areas like cards, panels and grouped lists. |
| `.text-body-large` | body/large/regular | 13/22 | 450 | -0.0025em | Our largest body text size, usually saved for elements like multiline text. |
| `.text-body-large-strong` | body/large/strong | 13/22 | 550 | -0.0025em | Our largest body text size, usually saved for elements like multiline text. |
| `.text-body-medium` | body/medium/regular | 11/16 | 450 | 0.005em | Our default text size for the majority of UI elements in the editor, such as inputs and buttons. |
| `.text-body-medium-strong` | body/medium/strong | 11/16 | 550 | 0.005em | Our default text size for the majority of UI elements in the editor, such as inputs and buttons. |
| `.text-body-small` | body/small/regular | 9/14 | 450 | 0.005em | Our smallest text size, primarily used by small UI elements like avatars and badges. |
| `.text-body-small-strong` | body/small/strong | 9/14 | 550 | 0.005em | Our smallest text size, primarily used by small UI elements like avatars and badges. |

Each class sets font-family, font-size, line-height, font-weight and letter-spacing. The same values are available as CSS variables, e.g. `var(--heading-large-font-size)`.

## Color

Rules:

- Use semantic tokens (var(--color-bg-*), --color-text-*, --color-icon-*, --color-border-*) in components. Never use primitives or hex values directly.
- Primitives (--color-<family>-<step>) only define what semantic tokens point to; add or change a semantic token in Figma rather than reaching for a primitive.
- Match the category to the property: bg-* for backgrounds, text-* for text, icon-* for icons, border-* for borders and dividers.
- Text and icons placed on a danger, warning or success fill use the matching on* tokens (e.g. --color-text-danger-ondanger on --color-bg-danger).
- Use inverse tokens together: --color-text-inverse / --color-icon-inverse on --color-bg-inverse.
- Interactive states use the -hover and -pressed variants of the same token, never a different hue.
- Dark mode: semantic tokens switch automatically inside [data-theme="dark"]; don't add separate dark styles.

### Semantic tokens

Use these in components. Values are `primitive (hex)`; dark mode applies inside `[data-theme="dark"]`.

### Primitives

Raw color scales from 100 (lightest) to 1000 (darkest). black and white are transparent scales (opacity steps); the others are solid. Some chromatic primitives have different values in dark mode. Values are light (and dark, where they differ).

| Family | CSS variable | Steps | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| black | `--color-black-<step>` | 100 #0000000d, 200 #0000001a, 300 #00000033, 400 #0000004d, 500 #00000080, 600 #000000cc, 700 #000000d9, 800 #000000e5, 900 #000000f2, 1000 #000000 | Black at increasing opacity — overlays, shadows, and neutral text/icon tints on light surfaces. |
| white | `--color-white-<step>` | 100 #ffffff0d, 200 #ffffff1a, 300 #ffffff33, 400 #ffffff66, 500 #ffffffb2, 600 #ffffffcc, 700 #ffffffd9, 800 #ffffffe5, 900 #fffffff2, 1000 #ffffff | White at increasing opacity — overlays and text/icon tints on dark or colored surfaces. |
| red | `--color-red-<step>` | 100 #fff5f5 / #fee7e7, 200 #ffe2e0 / #fccdca, 300 #ffc7c2 / #fbbcb6, 400 #ffafa3 / #fca397, 500 #f24822 / #e03e1a, 600 #dc3412 / #c4381c, 700 #bd2915 / #963323, 800 #9f1f18 / #7c2622, 900 #771208 / #54211c, 1000 #660e0b / #311817 | Danger and error colors. |
| orange | `--color-orange-<step>` | 100 #fff4e5 / #ffedd7, 200 #ffe0c2 / #fdd9b4, 300 #fcd19c / #fcc67f, 400 #ffc470 / #fcb34a, 500 #ffa629 / #de7d02, 600 #fc9e24 / #c86f04, 700 #f79722 / #ad5f05, 800 #dd7c0e / #985306, 900 #ce7012 / #673806, 1000 #8a480f / #371d06 | Accent orange (not yet used by any semantic token). |
| green | `--color-green-<step>` | 100 #ebffee / #ddfde2, 200 #cff7d3 / #beefc2, 300 #aff4c6 / #a1e8b9, 400 #85e0a3 / #79d297, 500 #14ae5c / #198f51, 600 #009951 / #078348, 700 #008043 / #0a5c35, 800 #036838 / #0a4c2d, 900 #024626 / #082618, 1000 #083a23 / #0b1e15 | Success colors. |
| yellow | `--color-yellow-<step>` | 100 #fffbeb / #fdf7dd, 200 #fff1c2 / #fbe8ad, 300 #ffe8a3 / #f9df90, 400 #ffd966 / #ffcd29, 500 #ffcd29 / #f3c11b, 600 #ffc21a / #f2b50d, 700 #fab815 / #e4a711, 800 #eba611 / #c58011, 900 #dd940e / #925711, 1000 #b86200 / #71440f | Warning colors. |
| grey | `--color-grey-<step>` | 100 #f5f5f5, 200 #e6e6e6, 300 #d9d9d9, 400 #b3b3b3, 500 #757575, 600 #444444, 700 #383838, 800 #2c2c2c, 900 #1e1e1e, 1000 #111111 | Solid neutrals for surfaces, borders and disabled states. |

## Spacing and radius

`--radius-full`: 9999px · `--radius-large`: 13px · `--radius-medium`: 6px · `--radius-none`: 0px · `--radius-small`: 2px · `--space-0`: 0px · `--space-1`: 2px · `--space-2`: 4px · `--space-3`: 8px · `--space-4`: 16px · `--space-5`: 24px · `--space-6`: 32px · `--space-7`: 40px

## Icons

The bulk of our icons are contained within a 24px frame, using 1px strokes with rounded caps, and can optionally come in a “small” size geared towards a 12px bounding box.

Library: [Iconoir](https://iconoir.com) (MIT), regular style — 869 icons, in one sprite, `/icons/iconoir.svg` (symbol ids `icon-<name>`). Inline the sprite once per page, then use the Icon Shell: `<svg class="icon icon--24" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-bell"></use></svg>` (styles: src/styles/components/icon.css).

| Size | Class | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32px | `.icon--32` | Large, standalone moments: empty states, onboarding, feature highlights. |
| 24px | `.icon--24` (default) | Default. Standalone icons in navigation, toolbars and cards. |
| 20px | `.icon--20` | List rows and menus next to body-large text. |
| 16px | `.icon--16` | Inside Buttons and Icon Buttons, inputs and dense UI next to body-medium text. |
| 12px | `.icon--12` | The “small” size: badges, tags and inline with body-small text. |

Rules:

- Inline the sprite (public/icons/iconoir.svg) once per page — at the top of <body>, or fetch and insert it like src/lib/icon.ts does — then use the Icon Shell: <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-<name>"></use></svg>. Set the size with icon--32, icon--24 (default), icon--20, icon--16 or icon--12.
- Only use icons from this catalog. To add one, add it in Figma and to tokens/icons.json, then run npm run tokens.
- Icons take the current text color; set it with a --color-icon-* token on the icon or its parent, never a hex value.
- Decorative icons get aria-hidden="true". An icon that is the only content of a control needs an aria-label on the control (see Icon Button).
- Buttons and Icon Buttons size their icons to 16px automatically.

## Components

### Button

Buttons let users initiate an action, acknowledge something, make a choice, or navigate. By default, our buttons are 24px tall, come in two styles (primary and secondary), and can optionally include an icon in front and in back.

Markup: `<button class="button button--<variant>" type="button">Label</button>` (styles: src/styles/components/button.css). Hover, pressed, focus and disabled states are built in.

| Class | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| `.button--primary` | The main action in a view, e.g. Save or Continue. Use one per view or panel. |
| `.button--secondary` | Supporting actions next to a primary button, e.g. Cancel or Back. |
| `.button--tertiary` | Low-emphasis actions in toolbars, lists and dense UI, where a fill would add noise. |
| `.button--danger` | Destructive actions that can't easily be undone, e.g. Delete. Confirm before acting. |
| `.button--success` | Positive, confirming actions, e.g. Approve or Publish. |

Rules:

- Use a <button class="button button--<variant>"> for actions and an <a class="button button--<variant>"> for navigation; never style a <div> as a button.
- Use one primary button per view or panel; pair it with secondary buttons for the other actions.
- Disable with the disabled attribute on <button> or aria-disabled="true" on links; every variant then shares the same disabled look.
- Write labels as short verbs (Save, Delete, Continue), not "OK" or "Click here".
- Icons are 16px Icon Shells (<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-<name>"></use></svg>) before or after the label; the button sizes them and they take the label's color. Icon-only actions use an Icon Button.

### Icon button

Icon buttons trigger an action with an icon alone, for compact toolbars and actions repeated on every row. They are 24px square, have no fill until hovered, and show an active fill while pressed or switched on.

Markup: `<button class="icon-button" type="button" aria-label="…"><svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-bell"></use></svg></button>` (styles: src/styles/components/icon-button.css).

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Default | No fill; the icon uses --color-icon-default. |
| Hover | --color-bg-hover fill under the pointer. |
| Active | --color-bg-pressed fill while pressed, or while a toggle is on (aria-pressed="true"). |
| Disabled | No fill and a dimmed icon; set the disabled attribute. |

Rules:

- Use <button class="icon-button" type="button" aria-label="…"> containing one Icon Shell (<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-<name>"></use></svg>); the button sizes it to 16px.
- Always give it an aria-label (and a matching title for a tooltip) — the icon alone has no accessible name.
- Use only icons whose meaning is clear without a label; otherwise use a Button with an icon and text.
- For on/off actions (e.g. Bold, Pin), toggle aria-pressed; the Active fill then shows the on state.

### Dropdown

Dropdowns let people pick one option from a list without taking up room on the page. They are 24px tall, with an optional 12px icon in front, and come with or without a stroke.

Markup: `<div class="dropdown"><select class="dropdown__select" aria-label="…">…</select><svg class="icon dropdown__chevron" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-nav-arrow-down"></use></svg></div>` (styles: src/styles/components/dropdown.css). enhanceDropdown() (src/lib/dropdown.ts) opens the options in an animated Menu; the select stays as the form value.

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Default | 1px --color-border-default stroke on --color-bg-default, value in --color-text-default. |
| Borderless | No stroke (Figma Stroke=False), for toolbars and dense rows. Add dropdown--borderless. |
| Focused | Keeps the stroke and adds a soft 1.4px --color-bg-secondary ring — for keyboard and pointer focus and while the list is open. It replaces the default focus outline. |
| Disabled | Value and chevron in --color-bg-disabled-secondary. Set disabled on the select. |

Rules:

- Use <div class="dropdown"> around a <select class="dropdown__select"> and the chevron <svg class="icon dropdown__chevron" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-nav-arrow-down"></use></svg>. Call enhanceDropdown() (src/lib/dropdown.ts) to open the options in a Menu; without it the native list opens.
- Use a dropdown to pick one of four or more options. For two or three, show them all; for on/off, use a Switch.
- Every dropdown needs a name: a visible <label for> or an aria-label on the select.
- Order options so people can scan them (by frequency or alphabetically) and preselect the most common one.
- Use dropdown--borderless only where many controls sit together, like toolbars; keep the stroke in forms.
- An optional icon before the value hints at what the list holds: add dropdown--icon and <svg class="icon dropdown__icon" aria-hidden="true">. The dropdown sizes icons to 12px.
- Disable with the disabled attribute on the select.

### Menu

Menus list actions or options in a panel that opens from a button or a dropdown. Items are 24px tall, with an optional 12px icon before the label and an arrow after it when they open a submenu.

Markup and behaviour: `createMenu(items, options)` in src/lib/menu.ts (styles: src/styles/components/menu.css); debounce helper in src/lib/debounce.ts.

| Item state | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Default | No fill, label in --color-text-default, icons in --color-icon-secondary (lead) and --color-icon-default (arrow). |
| Hover | --color-bg-hover fill, for the pointer and for keyboard focus alike, and on an item whose submenu is open. |
| Disabled | --color-bg-secondary fill, label and icons in --color-bg-disabled-secondary. Set aria-disabled="true". |

Rules:

- Use createMenu() (src/lib/menu.ts) for the markup and behaviour: <div class="menu" role="menu"> with <div class="menu__item" role="menuitem" tabindex="-1">. Add menu--floating for a menu that opens over content.
- Use a Menu for actions, and a Dropdown (which opens a Menu as a listbox) for picking a value.
- Keep labels short and on one line. Give every item a lead icon, or none.
- An arrow after the label means the item opens a submenu. Keep to one level of submenus.
- Submenus open when the pointer rests on their item for 300ms. The wait is a debounce: it restarts every time the pointer moves to another item, so passing over items doesn't flicker submenus open and shut. A click or Arrow Right opens them at once.
- Floating menus scale in from their trigger over 200ms with a strong ease-out and close faster (120ms). Opened from the keyboard, they appear instantly.
- Keep disabled items visible to show an action exists but isn't available now; use aria-disabled="true", not removal.

### Switch

Represent a physical toggle to turn a setting “on” or “off”. Unlike checkboxes, toggling a switch takes immediate effect without a need for additional confirmation steps (“save”).

Markup: `<button class="switch" type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="false" aria-label="…"><span class="switch__knob"></span></button>` (styles: src/styles/components/switch.css).

| State | Look |
| --- | --- |
| Off | Knob on the left over a --color-bg-hover track. aria-checked="false". |
| On | Knob slides right over a --color-bg-inverse track. aria-checked="true". |

Rules:

- Use <button class="switch" type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="false"> with <span class="switch__knob"></span> inside, and flip aria-checked in code — the styles follow it.
- Use a switch only for settings that apply immediately (theme, notifications). If the change waits for Save or Submit, use a checkbox.
- Every switch needs a name: a visible label linked with aria-labelledby, or an aria-label when the context makes it obvious.
- Name the setting, not the action: “Dark theme”, not “Turn dark theme on”. Don't add On/Off text next to the switch.
- In a settings row, put the label first and the switch at the end of the row.
- Disable with the disabled attribute.

### Tag

Tags label an item with a short status, category or count. They are 16px tall, come in five colors, and can be strong (filled) or outlined, with an optional 12px icon in front.

Markup: `<span class="tag tag--<variant>">Label</span>`, outlined with `tag--outline` (styles: src/styles/components/tag.css).

| Class | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| `.tag--default` | Neutral metadata: categories, versions, counts. |
| `.tag--inverted` | A neutral label that has to stand out, e.g. New or Beta. |
| `.tag--danger` | Errors and blocked states, e.g. Failed, Overdue, Blocked. |
| `.tag--success` | Positive or finished states, e.g. Done, Active, Paid. |
| `.tag--warning` | Needs attention but isn't broken, e.g. Pending, Expiring, Draft. |

Rules:

- Use <span class="tag tag--<variant>">Label</span>; add tag--outline for the outlined style (Figma Strong=False).
- Use a strong tag for the one status that matters most in a row or card, and outlined tags when several sit together, so they don't compete.
- Keep labels to one or two words. Tags don't wrap or truncate.
- Don't rely on color alone: the label itself must say the status.
- Tags aren't interactive. For an action, use a Button.
- An optional icon goes before the label: <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-<name>"></use></svg>. The tag sizes it to 12px and it takes the label's color.
